---
title: "Data files"
---

What ships inside the package, and what it downloads. Written against the files themselves;
where the package does not record a file's provenance, that is marked rather than guessed.

Downloads land in the atlas cache — see
[Data downloads and caching](../explanation/data-downloads-and-caching.qmd).

## Files shipped with the package

| File | Shape / dtype | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `allen_structure_tree.csv` | table | The Allen structure tree. **Provenance not recorded** |
| `franklin_paxinos_structure_tree.csv` | table | From Supplementary Data 2 of Chon et al. |
| `beryl.npy` | (306, 1) int32 | Allen ids defining the Beryl mapping, generated in MATLAB |
| `cosmos.npy` | (10, 1) int32 | Allen ids defining the Cosmos mapping, generated in MATLAB |
| `swanson_regions.npy` | (323,) int64 | Allen ids present in the Swanson flat map |
| `mappings.pqt` | (2655, 8) | The eight mappings, as indices into the lateralised structure tree |

Two counts look wrong and are not. `beryl.npy` holds **306** ids while the Beryl mapping
resolves to **308** distinct targets — the extra two are `void` and `root`. Likewise Cosmos:
10 ids, 12 targets. And `swanson_regions.npy` lists **323** ids while the Swanson image draws
**319** regions; not every listed id has a drawn patch.

`mappings.pqt` is generated by `BrainRegions._compute_mappings`; its columns are the eight
mapping names, the `-lr` suffix marking the lateralised variants.

## Files downloaded on demand

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `annotation_<res_um>.nrrd` | Region **indices** (not ids) per voxel, uint16, at the given isometric spacing |
| `average_template_<res_um>.nrrd` | The template image volume. **Not documented** |
| `annotation_<res_um>_lut_<LUT_VERSION>.npz` | Lookup table. **Not documented** |
| `FranklinPaxinos/annotation_<res_um>.npz` | Franklin–Paxinos region indices |
| `FranklinPaxinos/average_template_<res_um>.npz` | Allen DWI slices matching those annotations |
| `swansonpaths.json` | Vectorised Swanson flat map paths |
| `swanson2allen.npz` | **Not documented** — contents, author and purpose all unrecorded |
| `<flatmap_name>_<res_um>.nrrd` | **Not documented** — contents, author and purpose all unrecorded |
| `connectivity/allen_mouse_regionalized_connectivity.pqt` | Oh / Knox mesoscale connectivity, regionalized onto 291 Allen summary structures |
| `connectivity/allen_mouse_hierarchy_scores.pqt` | Harris cortico-thalamic hierarchy scores, 61 cortical and thalamic areas |

Note the annotation volumes store the region **index** — the position in the flattened
structure tree — not the Allen id. See
[The brain region hierarchy](../explanation/brain-region-hierarchy.qmd).

`swansonpaths.json` was traced from the BM3 rat flatmap foldout in Swanson (2004) *Brain Maps*,
3rd ed., using MATLAB's contour function, then simplified with Ramer–Douglas–Peucker. **The
code that did this is not in the repository** and its location is unrecorded.

## Where the external datasets come from

| Dataset | Source |
|---|---|
| Allen gene expression (AGEA) | Allen Institute, repackaged to a 200 µm grid on the `ibl-brain-wide-map-public` S3 bucket |
| MERFISH | Zhuang lab via an Allen release, on the same bucket under `atlas/merfish`. **No publication named** |
| Mesoscale connectivity | Oh et al. / Knox et al., regionalized by IBL |
| Cortico-thalamic hierarchy | Harris et al. |
| Streamlines | Allen cortical depth data, converted onto the atlas grid |
| Region meshes (`meshes.glb`) | Built from the Allen per-region `.obj` files — see [Convert Allen meshes to GLB](../how-to/convert-allen-meshes-to-glb.qmd) |

::: {.callout-note}
## Seven undocumented items

The package's own `Fixtures` section carries eight `TODO` markers; the gaps marked above are
the same ones. Nobody has recorded the provenance of `allen_structure_tree.csv`, the contents
of `average_template`, the annotation LUT, `swanson2allen.npz` or the flat map volumes, the
MERFISH citation, or where the Swanson vectorisation code lives.

If you know any of these, they are worth writing down here.
:::
